packageRules.description: youtarr's MariaDB: stay on the 11.8 LTS (supported into 2028). 13.0 is a rolling release with no further bug fixes, and MariaDB can't be downgraded after an upgrade. Move to the next LTS (12.3) deliberately.

linuxserver/lidarr publishes old 0.8.x builds as tags like 8.1.2135, which sort above the real 3.x releases. Renovate offered one as a 'major' update (Oct 2026); it was Lidarr 0.8, which has no Postgres support and started on an empty SQLite DB.

Label PRs by update type so the auto-review workflow can route them. Patch, digest, and minor updates auto-merge without a Claude review; automergeType=branch merges them straight to the base branch WITHOUT opening a PR (no PR = no notification email). If branch automerge can't complete, Renovate falls back to opening a labelled PR, which the auto-merge-simple workflow job then merges. Digest is grouped with patch here — matchUpdateTypes previously only listed 'patch', so digest-only bumps (e.g. #830) got no label at all and neither workflow job's label-gated 'if' ever matched, leaving them unrouted. The critical-infra groups below override this back to automerge=false and add the needs-review label so they always open a PR for review.

nginx uses odd minor versions (1.29, 1.31) for its mainline/development branch and even ones (1.30, 1.32) for stable. joshhawleygop.com serves from this image, so stay on stable: only offer even-minor releases.

A digest bump here is effectively a Postgres binary swap - CNPG rolls it onto replicas first via switchover, and can't do that safely without an already-healthy replica present. Automerged digest bumps for this image caused two separate shared-postgres outages (Sep 2026, #830 and #837): pg_basebackup refuses to join a replica whose image doesn't match the primary's, and the primary can only pick up the new image once a replica has already switched over to it - a deadlock when no replica is healthy.

prBodyNotes: Merging starts the node upgrade rollout immediately (Flux applies it within minutes). Servers upgrade first, then agents, one node at a time. Never merge a minor-version jump larger than one; check no Proxmox host maintenance is in progress.
